questions.q: In function first<T>(items: readonly T[]): T | undefined, what is T?
questions.explain: Angle brackets before the parameter list declare a type parameter. Each call fills it in, usually by inference from the arguments.
options: A variable that holds the first item
A type parameter: a placeholder for a type that the caller fills in
A type that means the same as any

questions.q: What is the type of title in const title = first(["Buy milk", "Call Ada"]);?

questions.q: When does the lesson pass the type yourself, as in first<string>([])?

options: Always; inference does not work for generics
When there is nothing to infer from, such as an empty array
When the function has more than one parameter

Generic maps only accept string keys

questions.q: Why does tsc reject item.id here?
questions.explain: Someone could call findById([1, 2, 3], 1). Without a rule, TypeScript lets you do almost nothing with T. The fix is a constraint: T extends { id: number }.
options: Because find cannot be used in generic functions
T could be any type, such as number, which has no id
Because the return type should be T[]

questions.q: What does <T extends { id: number }> mean?
questions.explain: A constraint sets a rule. A task or a user both fit, and the result is still the full T, so findById(tasks, 2)?.title works.
options: T must be exactly { id: number } and nothing more
T can be any type, as long as it has at least a numeric id
T is a class that inherits from another class

questions.q: With function findById<T extends { id: number }>(items: readonly T[], id: number): T | undefined, which call does tsc reject?
questions.explain: Numbers have no id property, so they break the constraint. Any object with a numeric id is fine, whatever other properties it has.

questions.q: For type Task = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean }, what is keyof Task?
questions.explain: keyof T is the union of T's property names. The types of the values are T[K].

questions.q: With function pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(items: readonly T[], key: K): T[K][], what is the type of pluck(tasks, "done") when tasks have a boolean done?
questions.explain: K is "done", and T[K] is the type of that property, boolean. So the result is an array of booleans.

questions.q: With type Result<T, E = string> = ..., what does Result<number> mean?
questions.explain: E = string is a default type parameter. Leave E out and it is string. Pass a second type when you need a different error, such as "not-found" | "suspended".

questions.q: Why does ok(value) return Result<T, never>?
questions.explain: never is the type with no values, and it fits every other type. So ok(port) can be returned from a function whose return type is Result<number, string> or any other error type.
options: So that it can never be called
A success can never hold an error, so it fits any Result<T, E>
It makes the function throw on failure

questions.q: parsePort returns Result<number>. Which code does tsc accept?
questions.explain: You must check ok before reading value or error, and each exists only on its own side. So you cannot forget the failure case.

questions.q: What does returning a Result give you, compared with throwing an error for an invalid port?
questions.explain: A thrown error is invisible in the function's type, so a caller can forget to catch it. A Result forces the check. @zudojs/schema's safeParse works the same way, with a success flag.
options: It makes the function run faster
The failure is part of the return type, so every caller must handle it before using the value
It hides the error from the caller

questions.q: Why are the MemoryRepository methods async, even though a Map answers instantly?

So that they run in parallel
A real database will not answer instantly, so a database version can replace it without changing the code that uses it
To make the repository slower for testing
